title: Hubble captures view of “Mystic Mountain”
caption: 'Mystic Mountain' in the Carina Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Carina Nebula, HH 901, HH 902 · constellation Carina · about 7500 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, M. Livio and the Hubble 20th Anniversary Team (STScI)

recognition.text: Ranked #38 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A craggy peak wrapped in wispy clouds rises through this Hubble image, like a scene out of a fantasy novel. It is the top of a three-light-year-tall pillar of gas and dust, and it is being eaten away by the brilliant light of nearby stars. Streamers of hot gas flow off its ridges, and veils of starlit dust float around its peaks.

The pillar sits inside the Carina Nebula, a turbulent stellar nursery 7500 light-years away. Scorching radiation and fast winds of charged particles from super-hot newborn stars are shaping and compressing it, prompting new stars to form inside. Its densest parts are resisting erosion.

It is also under attack from within. Young stars buried in the pillar fire off jets. One pair shoots out both ways from the pedestal at the top, and another from a peak near the center. These jets, HH 901 and HH 902, are signs of star birth, launched by discs of gas and dust feeding the stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.39 x 1.28 arcminutes) and distance (7500 light years), the frame spans roughly 3 × 2.8 light-years. Its light set out about 7,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3. Blue shows the glow of oxygen, green shows hydrogen and nitrogen, and red shows sulfur.
understand.eye: The colors isolate light from particular elements, so they map chemistry rather than the hues an eye would see.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA, M. Livio and the Hubble 20th Anniversary Team (STScI)
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: This image was released to celebrate 20 years since Hubble was launched and placed into orbit around the Earth.
alt: A craggy pillar of gas and dust with wispy clouds around its peaks and thin jets of gas streaming from its tips.
